issues.legal_issue: A compromise decree made before the narrowing amendment to the decree-registration exception remains within that exception even when it deals with immovable property beyond the subject matter of the suit.
material_facts: The decree was based on a compromise in a suit concerning a disputed portion of a larger area of coal-bearing land.
The compromise decree also dealt with the parties’ rights and obligations concerning the larger area beyond the disputed portion.
The decree was made before the statutory amendment that narrowed the exception for compromise decrees.
issues.conclusion: The decree-registration exception applicable before the amendment covered the compromise decree even to the extent that it dealt with property outside the subject matter of the suit.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 17(2)(vi) of the Indian Registration Act, 1908, as it stood before the amendment effective on 1 April 1930, a decree or order of court was excepted from the registration requirements in clauses (b) and (c) of section 17(1), including a compromise decree dealing with immovable property beyond the subject matter of the suit. The Court relied on Hemanta Kumari Debi v. Midnapur Zamindari Co.

predicates.appeal_contests_registration_of_compromi: A party in an appeal challenged the use of a compromise decree on the ground that it was unregistered.
predicates.decree_predates_narrowing_amendment: The court made the compromise decree before a later amendment narrowed the registration exception for compromise decrees.
predicates.decree_covers_property_outside_suit: The compromise decree dealt with immovable property beyond the property that was the subject of the suit.
predicates.decree_would_otherwise_require_registrat: The decree concerns rights in immovable property of a kind that would otherwise require registration.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges the registration of a pre-amendment compromise decree that extends beyond the suit property, the decree exception covers that additional property if the document would otherwise require registration.

issues.legal_issue: A compromise decree that provides for an underlease only upon a future payment does not itself create a present lease requiring registration as a lease, and may be exempt from registration as a court decree.
material_facts: A compromise decree provided that one set of parties would hold disputed land as tenants under another set of parties, with revised royalty obligations.
The arrangement was conditional on payment of a sum to the original lessor within a specified period; until payment, the parties could not execute the decree or take possession of the disputed land.
The decree also provided for execution of further lease documents, or for the compromise document itself to operate on the stated terms if those further documents were not executed.
The appeal challenged the use of the compromise decree in a claim for royalties and cesses on the ground that the decree was unregistered.
issues.conclusion: The contingent arrangement was not a lease under section 17(1)(d), because it did not create a present and immediate interest in the land. Although it fell within section 17(1)(b), it was exempt from registration under section 17(2)(vi), so the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(7) of the Indian Registration Act, 1908, includes an agreement to lease within the term “lease,” but, as explained in Hemanta Kumari Debi v. Midnapur Zamindari Co., an agreement for a lease must effect an actual demise and create a present and immediate interest in land. The conditional arrangement therefore did not fall within section 17(1)(d). It was nevertheless within section 17(1)(b) and exempt as a court decree under section 17(2)(vi).

predicates.decree_records_immovable_property_arrang: The compromise decree records an arrangement concerning rights in immovable property.
predicates.proposed_underlease_depends_on_future_pa: The decree makes the proposed underlease effective only if a party makes a required payment within a stipulated period.
predicates.possession_or_enforcement_is_barred_unti: The decree prevents possession or enforcement of the arrangement until the required payment is made.

issues.definition: If an appeal challenges an unregistered compromise decree concerning immovable property and the proposed underlease depends on payment that must precede possession or enforcement, the decree is exempt from registration.
